slices.scope: Classify the connected sub_821A5080 -> sub_821A3BA0 path, including outgoing boundaries and unresolved receiver populations.
slices.excludes: No native changes, broader closure classification, inventory regeneration or parent completion.
steps: Verify the caller/callee edge in generated-call-edges.csv and locate both generated bodies; check available Ghidra exports when useful.
Record seed justification, every direct outgoing edge, eight frame indirect sites and the bucket-dispatch site. If the counts differ, report the discrepancy instead of forcing the count.
Produce contract.csv with instruction/source locators, guard, reads, writes, owner/lifetime, classification and evidence IDs. Preserve unresolved targets as explicit follow-ups.
Write results.md and a submission JSON. Classify only this path; keep the parent open.

cases.description: Both functions have incoming-path witnesses and outgoing-boundary dispositions.
Every indirect site is enumerated; unproven receiver targets remain unresolved with next queries.
Simulation/CPU writes and shared utilities are distinguished from render consumption with source evidence.

stop_conditions: Do not expand beyond the two selected functions; return follow-ups for callees.

slices.scope: Implement a bounded three-frame final-host capture with unique output names and truthful sequence/time metadata, preserving disabled and one-shot behavior.
slices.excludes: No gameplay boot, visual parity claim, partial-scene relabeling, broad host redesign or parent completion.
steps: Read both host composition/capture paths. Record their frame identity, capture timing and ownership contract in Epistemic before editing.
Add the smallest bounded capture API/policy that handles three outputs, exhaustion, repeated sequence IDs and unique filenames. Repeated source sequences must remain truthful.
Implement metadata and failure handling for missing images, collisions and write errors; preserve capture-off and default one-shot behavior.
Add independent policy/host tests, build and run the supplemental host test, then run the full offline gate. Request coordinator access before GPU validation.
Submit patch in the isolated checkout with contract.csv, results.md and result JSON; report gameplay/pause/loading visual acceptance as not_run.

cases.description: Exactly three outputs are produced and later requests are exhausted.
Manifest index, sequence, time, extent, backend and final-composition kind describe the actual frame; repeated sequences remain truthful.
Disabled capture does no readback/file work; default one-shot still works.
Absent image, name collision and write error have tested bounded behavior without silent overwrite.
Gameplay/pause/loading visual examples remain pending until a milestone boot.

stop_conditions: Escalate if a host cannot expose final composition or sequence identity.
Ask coordinator to expand ownership before editing any additional file.
Do not fabricate distinct sequence IDs to satisfy a uniqueness test.

slices.scope: Independently audit the first-wave packet prerequisites, baseline identity, file ownership and rejection tests.
slices.excludes: No source edits, ledger mutations, automatic readiness grants or renderer parent completion.
steps: Inspect both renderer packet scopes, input locators and allowed-file sets against their actual source contracts.
Verify the pinned baseline includes dirty and untracked inputs and that implementation requires a matching isolated checkout.
Run dispatch rejection tests and coverage validation; inspect whether tests exercise real rejection paths.
Publish readiness findings and explicit gaps with evidence IDs. The coordinator alone decides readiness.

cases.description: Every first-wave input and prerequisite locator exists or has an explicit blocker.
Allowed writes are disjoint and both host headers are included in capture scope.
Tests reject stale input/source, dependency violations, overlap, out-of-scope changes, self-review, altered artifacts and stale offline reports.

stop_conditions: Report missing proof as a blocker; successful packet rendering alone is not readiness.
